sources.entry: Resume Claim Guard - Open-source agent skill that writes a job-tailored resume from confirmed facts only, then audits claims and previews interview follow-ups. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: An agent skill (also usable as a plain chat prompt) that tailors a resume to a job description using only facts the user confirms, then audits each claim and previews interview follow-ups.
use_cases: tailor a resume to a specific job posting without inventing experience
check whether resume verbs and numbers overstate what I actually did
prepare answers for likely interviewer follow-up questions
turn an AI-edited resume back into confirmed facts
keep one consistent story across several resume versions sent to different companies
rehearse how to answer gaps between the job requirements and my experience
how_to_run: Web chat: open PROMPT.md, copy the whole prompt into ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Kimi or Doubao, then paste the job description and your resume
Quick start: copy the English or Chinese one-sentence prompt from the README and paste it with the job description and resume
Claude Code: tell it to clone the repo into ~/.claude/skills/resume-claim-guard
Codex: tell it to clone the repo into ~/.codex/skills/resume-claim-guard
WorkBuddy: tell it to clone the repo into ~/.workbuddy/skills/resume-claim-guard
Other SKILL.md-compatible agents: place the repository in that agent's skills directory
stack: Markdown prompts and SKILL.md skill format
notable: Asks clarifying questions one requirement at a time before writing anything, and waits for the user to confirm a fact list
Separates personal role (participated, owned, led) from delivery stage (plan, prototype, launched, with results) so verbs cannot exceed the facts
Tags each sentence in a line-by-line audit as confirmed, supported, needs-source, inference or rejected
Gives a suggestion such as apply, apply with supplements, apply cautiously, or do not apply with a reason, rather than a numeric match score
Ships a Chinese-first README with a short English quick start
caveats: README is mostly in Chinese; the full prompt and examples are Chinese, with only a short English quick start
Does not search for jobs, auto-fill applications, submit resumes, or export PDFs
The README says the Doubao and Qianwen custom agents were taken offline on 2026-07-15, so the one-sentence chat prompt is the fallback for those tools
